subject: Protecting launch: short-term burst credit + rate hedge
messages:
From: Maya Cole <maya.cole@skylark.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skylark.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Short window uplift for launch + any credit options?

Hi Grace,

We’re a few days out from Skylark’s public beta launch (Nov 18) and we’re seeing traffic projections that outstrip our committed tier for a short window. Can Redwood provide a short-term uplift (headroom) for the launch week and/or a burst credit allowance? We want to avoid throttling and keep latency predictable.

Key asks:
- ~3M extra tokens over 7–10 days (estimate, could be front-loaded)
- Prefer a short-term price cap or blended rate rather than paygo spikes
- Ability to convert unused portion into commit credit if we decide to expand

We’re on the Growth plan, and Laura has been our rep for onboarding; cc’d her and procurement so we can get PO details if we proceed.

Appreciate any quick options — launch timeline is tight.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Cole
Head of Product, Skylark.ai

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the heads up and the projection. We can absolutely help protect the launch. I’m looping in Ben (sales) and Karthik (pricing/ops) to propose a short path that balances cost certainty and rapid execution.

Two quick questions to size the offer:
1) Is the 3M tokens primarily generation (output) or embedding/lookup volume?
2) Do you need burst capacity in a single region (us-west) or multi-region?

I’ll ask Ben to get a nominal offer over to you today; if procurement needs a PO template we can attach it.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short window uplift for launch + any credit options?

Hi Maya / team —

Thanks — scope makes sense. Based on your projection and a typical generation-heavy profile, here’s a rapid, executable option we can sign off on this afternoon:

Offer (72-hour approval window):
- Short-term burst pool: 3,000,000 tokens usable over a 10-day window (Nov 16–25)
- One-time uplift fee: $6,000 (covers guaranteed capacity reservation + minor provisioning)
- Blended rate hedge: if your usage exceeds the pool, overrun tokens billed at a capped rate of $0.0045/token for the remainder of the month (instead of our standard paygo $0.006/token)
- Conversion option: any unused tokens in the burst pool may be converted into committed monthly credits at 70% of list price if you convert within 30 days after the window

Operational notes:
- We’ll provision the burst in the us-west region by default; multi-region is possible but adds provisioning lead time (let us know).
- We’ll enable a soft-alarm at 80% consumption and a hard throttle at 100% of the pool; you can request manual override during the window.
- Attachment: draft burst proposal and an example PO template (see skylark-burst-proposal-20261111.pdf).

If that looks reasonable we can get a short amendment signed (DocuSign) and provision the pool same-day.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Ben / Grace,

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement reviewed and asks two small clarifications before we sign:
1) Billing structure: we prefer the one-time uplift fee to be invoiced on the same PO as the conversion/commit option (single invoice flow). Is Redwood able to accommodate a single PO/invoice for the uplift fee and any converted credits?
2) Liability cap: can you confirm there won’t be any retroactive overage adjustments beyond the capped overrun rate laid out in the proposal? We need a clear ceiling for our finance team.

We’ve attached a PO draft for your legal/ops team to check — skylark-po-draft-20261112.pdf. Otherwise, we’re comfortable with the token quantities and timing. If those two items are okay we can sign the DocuSign today and issue PO immediately.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Skylark.ai

Subject: Re: Protecting launch: short-term burst credit + rate hedge

Hi — quick answers:

1) Single-invoice flow: Yes — Redwood can accept a single PO that covers the one-time uplift fee and any converted credits; we’ll route to finance to ensure the invoice references the PO number.

2) Liability cap: Confirmed — the only post-facto billing beyond the burst pool would be tokens consumed beyond the pool during the month, and those will be billed at the capped overrun rate in Ben’s proposal. We will not retroactively apply higher paygo rates or add undisclosed surcharges. We’ll include a clause in the amendment that explicitly states the ceiling.

Next steps:
- Ben / Legal to drop a short amendment (DocuSign) reflecting the uplift fee, capped overrun rate, conversion flow, and the single-po invoicing clause.
- Once signed, ops will provision the 3M token pool in us-west and turn on 80% soft alerts.

Ben — can you kick off the DocuSign? I’ll coordinate with ops for provisioning as soon as it’s signed.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
